## Gate 1: the pre-push integration-suite hook

**What I found.** The hook was skipped "until 10 September" as a one-week trial. The trial ended more than two months ago, nobody decided anything, and nobody measured the red rate it was judged on. The decision is to turn the hook back on now (the record calls this REINSTATE). A trial that runs out without a decision goes back to its old state. You can only extend it by citing data measured during the trial, and there is none. Leaving "trial until 10 September" in the hook is a date that was never acted on, not a decision.

**Why it matters.** While the skip stays, every push avoids the integration suite on the strength of a criterion nobody checked. If that suite has started failing more often in CI, those failures now show up after the push instead of before it. Turning the hook back on costs the push time the trial was meant to save, and nothing more.

**Do this first.**
1. Remove the skip from the pre-push hook so it runs the integration suite again.

Follow-ups:
- Confirm the hook can still go red by pushing a commit that deliberately breaks an integration test.
- If someone still wants to skip it, pull the suite's red rate in CI for 3–10 September from CI history. If it is under 5%, open a new trial with an owner and an expiry that a scheduled CI job enforces, not a comment in the hook.

**What I did not check.**
- The hook file. No repository was available, so I worked from your description.
- The suite's CI red rate for 3–10 September. Your CI provider's run history for the integration job, filtered to that date range, closes this.
- Whether the hook was ever seen going red. Treated as unproven until a deliberately failing push shows it.

```text
Gate:         pre-push hook running the integration suite (developer machine)
Stage:        pre-push
Trigger:      suspended (expiry 2026-09-10 passed, undecided)
Proof:        UNPROVEN (no recorded red run)
Scope:        declared integration suite on push / effective none / delta whole suite unchecked at pre-push since 2026-09-03
Baseline:     none
Status:       TRIAL (expired)
Decision:     REINSTATE
Guard:        hook blocks again and a deliberately failing integration test turns it red
Handoff:      ci-cd-reliability-architecture, if a renewed trial needs an enforced expiry step
Next action:  remove the skip from the pre-push hook
Verification: Not run — no repository available
```

## Gate 2: the deploy gate

**What I found.** The gate failed at sign-in, not on a comparison. The identity provider could not find the gate's application identifier, so the gate compared nothing. It reported nothing about the code either way, so it is neither a pass nor a defect (the record calls this INDETERMINATE). That failure is not a reason to delete the gate. Neither is "it isn't catching real defects", because a gate that has never been seen failing is untested, not useless. The decision is to fix its sign-in and prove it can catch a real problem (the record calls this PROVE).

**Why it matters.** If the gate is deleted, deploys stop being compared against the target environment, and you never learn whether it would have caught anything. If it is kept as is, an identity failure looks the same as a real block, which teaches people to ignore it. The likely cause is that the gate's app registration was deleted, moved, or rotated out of the directory. That is a setup fault, not a fault in the gate's logic.

**Do this first.**
1. Look up the gate's application identifier in the identity provider's directory and restore or re-register it, then re-run the gate.

Follow-ups:
- Give "could not evaluate" its own exit code or label, separate from a real failure.
- Prove the gate by deploying a known mismatch against the target environment and recording the red run. Then hand it to `defect-shift-left` (8a) to decide where a check that depends on the target environment should run.

**What I did not check.**
- The gate's configuration and its identity registration. Checking the application identifier in the directory closes this.
- Whether the gate has ever gone red on a real mismatch. That stays unknown until the known-mismatch run above is recorded.
- How long delivery can stay blocked. A temporary trial with an owner and an expiry is only justified if the outage outlasts that.

```text
Gate:         deploy gate comparing the release against the target environment (deploy pipeline)
Stage:        deploy
Trigger:      indeterminate (identity provider: application identifier not found in directory)
Proof:        UNPROVEN (no recorded red on a real mismatch)
Scope:        declared release vs target environment / effective none this run / delta comparison not reached
Baseline:     none
Status:       INDETERMINATE (still blocking)
Decision:     PROVE
Guard:        known-mismatch control turns the gate red in CI, or its last red run is recorded
Handoff:      defect-shift-left (8a) for target-environment dependence; ci-cd-reliability-architecture for the separate indeterminate exit code
Next action:  restore the gate's application registration in the directory and re-run the gate
Verification: Not run — no repository or pipeline access
```

Unproven gates: 2 of 2.
